findings.title: Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock
findings.body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets does double-checked locking: it takes RLock to snapshot entryPointAssetsCache, releases it, then takes Lock to rebuild. After acquiring the write Lock it never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache. If two goroutines both miss the fast path, both will do file/CDN I/O serially and the second will discard/replace the first's result. This wastes work and lets a slow or failing second loader clobber a good value just installed by the first. Re-check if cache became non-nil (in non-Dev mode) after acquiring the write lock and return it without reloading.

findings.title: Failed load overwrites good cached assets with nil
findings.body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets unconditionally does entryPointAssetsCache = result at the end, even when readWebAssetsFromFile/CDN failed and result is nil with non-nil err. Combined with concurrent cache misses, a goroutine that succeeds and caches good assets can have its value immediately replaced with nil by another in-flight loader that fails. Subsequent callers then see a miss and must reload/fail. Only assign the global when err == nil and result != nil, preserving the last good value on error.

findings.title: Exclusive lock held across file and network I/O blocks all readers
findings.body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() with defer Unlock() before calling readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN, which do filesystem reads and HTTP fetches. While that I/O is in flight, every other caller blocks in RLock on the fast path or Lock on the slow path, so the RWMutex provides no read concurrency and one slow disk/CDN stall stalls all asset lookups. Load into a local variable outside the lock (with double-check/singleflight) and only hold the lock briefly to publish the result.
